fable.w: This section is a funding table authorizing military personnel appropriations, with line-item adjustments such as retaining Global Hawk and National Guard force structure. A tempting reading might treat the National Guard references as state involvement, but they are only budget lines. No outside party is consulted, no hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is provided.

qwen_block.w: This section is a table of appropriations for military personnel and related funding adjustments. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal entities in a federal decision-making process. The text merely lists budget figures and line items.
qwen_block.s: SEC. 4401. MILITARY PERSONNEL(In Thousands of Dollars) ItemFY 2013 RequestConference Authorized MILITARY PERSONNEL135,111,799135,777,368

opus.w: This section is an appropriations table listing requested and authorized funding amounts for military personnel. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to consult on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision. The mention of the National Guard is just a budget line, not a requirement to consult with states.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a table of appropriations for military personnel and related items. It lists funding amounts but does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. The mention of National Guard members refers only to funding for their allowances or force structure, not to their involvement in federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "National Guard" or "Air National Guard" members are outside the federal government because they are state-based. However, the text only lists funding amounts for personnel and force structure; it does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or decision-making involving these groups or any other outside parties. It is purely an appropriations table.
